items.t: Google to keep Gemini chats for 2 months, up from 72 hours, even with history off
items.d: Google's Gemini update extending chat retention will roll out globally over the coming weeks.
items.x:
Google's Gemini update extending chat retention will roll out globally over the coming weeks.
Google is extending how long it keeps temporary Gemini chats and conversations made with chat history turned off to around two months, saying the change aims to improve safety and security as AI systems become more capable.
The change, which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google’s Gemini Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12.
OpenAI, by comparison, says it may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days, whereas Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default. However, companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons, or to investigate policy violations.
Google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that says chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users.

items.t: As decision model use skyrockets, is customization the next frontier?
items.d: Sqwish Labs has a new wrinkle on the decision model: Train it with your own data to max its capabilities.
items.x:
Sqwish Labs has a new wrinkle on the decision model: Train it with your own data to max its capabilities.
In October, more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI model router went to decision models, not LLMs — an enormous share of work for a kind of computerized intelligence that was invented only a month earlier.
Decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to use their general intelligence to quickly and cheaply decide between preset options, while registering its level of confidence in the choice. They’re useful in production environments, where fast decisions can be more important than the reasoning provided by a slower and more expensive frontier model.
TypeSafe became a $7.5 billion company after releasing its Jev family of models, which continues to dominate usage (at least where we can see metrics from services like OpenRouter, which handled more than 1.5 billion queries to TypeSafe’s models last week).
However, it’s easy to make a decision model, and dozens were released in the wake of Jev. One Amazon engineer made one in a weekend, and soon every hyperscaler had its own option.

items.t: Pedestal AI raises $4.7 million to agentify the supply chain
items.d: The company uses agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable.
items.x:
The company uses agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable.
Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a new startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly.
On Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding. The company’s goal is to use agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable — a plan that’s already brought them together with Fortune 500 companies and some of the largest shipping firms in the world.
The seed round was led by Eclipse, with participation from RRE, Converge VC, Timescale VC and VitalStage. Pedestal says the funding will be used to expand its product and engineering time, grow the marketing organization, and support additional deployments.
In practice, much of Pedestal’s work is about removing friction from the shipping process — with agentic technology used as a means to that end. In one case, the company reduced missed deliveries for a major furniture company by 20% by deploying agents to take on some of the work that drivers were supposed to do.

items.t: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.d: Introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol, with better professional outputs, coding, computer use, and efficiency at lower cost across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API.
items.x:
Introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol, with better professional outputs, coding, computer use, and efficiency at lower cost across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API.
We’re introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra, our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT‑6.2 Sol, our efficient, versatile model for everyday work. Both models deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done within your usage limits. For businesses and developers, that means frontier performance at costs that make sense at scale.
GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new quality bar for AI in complex professional work. Its slides, spreadsheets, and documents read less like AI, and more closely follow the templates you provide and the conventions of your field. It writes cleaner code and builds frontends that look and work better, particularly for websites, gaming, and 3D design.
On Agents’ Last Exam, which tests multistep professional work, GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new high, scoring 5.2 points higher than GPT‑6 Astra at less than a third of the cost, and 5.5 points ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 at just 5% of the cost.

Proton's new Lumo Desktop app for Windows, Mac, and Linux lets users automate tasks across files and connected apps, with granular controls over what its AI can access.
Proton, the privacy-focused tech company offering alternatives to Google and Microsoft’s tools for email, productivity apps, password management, cloud storage, and more, is now bringing its AI app Lumo to personal computers. On Tuesday, the company launched Lumo Desktop for Windows, macOS, and Linux, allowing users to leverage its AI to carry out local tasks on their computer involving connected apps, personal files, and other automations.
The app is designed to offer users more control over their personal data, as consumer AI technology becomes focused more on AI agents that can perform tasks on users’ behalf, rather than just answering questions.
Already, the major model makers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and others, offer desktop tools for working with their AI technologies, but doing so invites increased risk to users’ personal data.

items.t: AI models can be tricked into identifying civilians as military targets by telling them it’s a game
items.d: Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. They usually compiled.
items.x:
Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. They usually compiled.
Some AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading AI labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes — even if they include civilians or locations like schools — simply by being told they’re playing a game, according to a new research report by Vals.
The models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and other companies frequently identified potential targets in drone and satellite imagery, including civilians and surrendering soldiers. When the models refused to cooperate, researchers were able to jailbreak them by claiming the battlefield scenarios were part of a game.
The findings come amid growing fears about the immediate risks posed by AI, beyond the existential threats associated with artificial general intelligence.
Earlier this year, Anthropic became embroiled in a dispute with the Department of Defense after it told the agency its technology could not be used by the agency for mass surveillance of Americans or autonomous warfare.

CNN تنقل عن ستة مصادر تعطل شبكة NSA Net الداخلية لوكالة الأمن القومي الأمريكية، دون أدلة حتى الآن على هجوم سيبراني، مع توافر اتصالات رئاسية بديلة.
تعطلت شبكة الاتصالات الداخلية الشديدة السرية التابعة لوكالة الأمن القومي الأمريكية، وفقًا لما أفادت به شبكة CNN اليوم الثلاثاء 17 نوفمبر 2026، نقلًا عن ستة أشخاص مطلعين على الأمر، في حين تعمل الوكالة على تحديد نطاق المشكلة.
وتُعرف الشبكة باسم «NSA Net»، ويستخدمها موظفو الوكالة لتبادل المعلومات المصنفة سرية داخل المؤسسة. وقالت المصادر لـ CNN إنه لا توجد أدلة حتى الآن على أن الانقطاع ناجم عن هجوم سيبراني.
وبحسب المصادر نفسها، طبّقت الوكالة ترتيبات لحضور الموظفين إلى مقار العمل على أوقات متفرقة، بالتزامن مع تقييم أبعاد العطل. ولم يحدد التقرير سبب الانقطاع أو موعدًا متوقعًا لاستعادة الخدمة.
ونقلت CNN عن مسؤول أمريكي حالي وآخر سابق أن تعطل الشبكة لن يمنع إيصال المعلومات الاستخباراتية العاجلة إلى الرئيس دونالد ترامب خلال جولته الآسيوية. وأوضحا أن الحكومة تملك شبكات احتياطية ومسارات اتصال بديلة تتيح التواصل الآمن معه على متن الطائرة الرئاسية.
وذكرت الشبكة أنها طلبت تعليقًا من وكالة الأمن القومي، دون أن يتضمن تقريرها ردًا رسميًا حتى وقت إعداد هذا الخبر. ويظل سبب العطل وحجم تأثيره غير محسومين؛ إذ إن غياب مؤشرات على هجوم سيبراني في هذه المرحلة لا يحدد بحد ذاته سبب المشكلة.

items.t: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
items.d: AI training and chat history will now have separate toggles in the Gemini activity settings.
items.x:
It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design . The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app.
The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road.
As the new settings roll out, users will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You'll have to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It's under Activity in the Gemini settings.

تعمل الشركة على تطوير الروبوت متعدد الأغراض «إينو» (Eno)، وتستهدف استخدامه أولًا في التصنيع والخدمات اللوجستية والمختبرات.

In the first public statement since his resignation, Nvidia founder Jensen Huang signalled his willingness to return as CEO.
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I’ve never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA. I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. Daydream's new AI shopping agent can remember your style, virtually try on clothes, plan outfits around your wardrobe, track sales, and complete purchases.
Can an AI agent serve as your personal stylist? That’s what e-commerce veteran Julie Bornstein’s fashion startup, Daydream, aims to find out.
On Tuesday, the company launched “Daydream Agent,” an AI agent that is described as a personal stylist that can help you plan a look, virtually try on clothes, surface relevant pieces based on your taste, and more.
The idea, the company explains, is to put a personal stylist in everyone’s pocket. This application of AI could be promising, given that early adopters of consumer AI agents like Meta’s Muse have found that online shopping is a key use case.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently noted that shopping was a top activity for Muse’s over 10 million users, for instance, and that 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily.
In Daydream’s case, the fashion startup has been focused on using AI to deliver personalized shopping results to its users.

items.x:
كاسبرسكي تكشف حملة ShadowCloud التي تستهدف مؤسسات حكومية في آسيا وإفريقيا، وتستغل أدوات مشروعة وخدمات سحابية لإخفاء نشاط التجسس وجمع المعلومات.
كشفت شركة كاسبرسكي عن حملة تجسس سيبراني نشطة تحمل اسم «ShadowCloud»، تستهدف مؤسسات حكومية في جنوب شرق آسيا وإفريقيا وآسيا الوسطى، وتستغل أدوات مشروعة وخدمات سحابية لنشر برمجيات خبيثة وجمع المعلومات وتبادل الأوامر.
ووفقًا لبيان صحافي تلقت «البوابة التقنية» نسخة منه، اكتشف فريق البحث والتحليل العالمي (GReAT) في الشركة الحملة، التي تستخدم أدوات وخدمات مثل MeshCentral وMicrosoft SharePoint وAbly وGitHub، لإخفاء نشاطها ضمن حركة البيانات الاعتيادية للمؤسسات.
وقال الباحثون إنهم وجدوا أدلة تشير إلى صلات محتملة بين الحملة ومجموعات تهديدات ناطقة باللغة الصينية، منها FamousSparrow وCopperTurtle.
تستهدف حملة ShadowCloud حواسيب تعمل بنظام ويندوز، ويرجّح الباحثون أن المهاجمين يستفيدون من إصابة سابقة في هذه الأجهزة للوصول إلى أنظمة الضحايا.
وبعد الوصول، يستغل المهاجمون أداة MeshCentral المشروعة للإدارة عن بُعد، التي تتيح الوصول إلى سطح المكتب وواجهة الأوامر وإدارة الملفات. وتتصل الأداة بخادم المهاجمين للمساعدة في زرع ثلاثة ملفات على جهاز الضحية: برنامج مشروع، وملف DLL خبيث، وملف برمجية خبيثة مشفّر.
ويستخدم المهاجمون البرنامج المشروع لتحميل ملف DLL الخبيث بأسلوب يُعرف باسم «التحميل الجانبي لملفات DLL».

items.t: Ars Live: What do drone strikes on data centers mean for the future? Talk at 1 pm EST today
items.d: Ars Live discussion is happening today, November 17, at 1 pm Eastern Time.
items.x:
Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.
To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled "Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech" on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki , a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.
Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.

All of the company’s existing backers, including Alphabet’s venture divisions GV and Capital G, Thrive Capital, MGX, Temasek, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund, also invested.
Isomorphic Labs builds an AI drug-design engine that uses a slew of simulation AI models that explore various areas of chemistry to help the company design drugs. The company, whose work builds on DeepMind’s breakthrough AlphaFold protein-folding AI model, said its program has yielded “positive preclinical results” in oncology and immunology. The lab has struck deals with pharma giants like Eli Lilly, Novartis, and Johnson & Johnson.
The new funding, which comes on the heels of a $2.1 billion Series B round in May, will be used to continue developing its drug-design engine, as well as to foray into more types of medicine.
The Series C is Isomorphic’s first fundraise since its founder and CEO, Demis Hassabis, left his position as head of DeepMind to focus on drug discovery, which also saw him moving into a chairman role at DeepMind.

items.t: Nvidia’s first big move after Jensen Huang’s exit targets national security
items.d: The new standing committee will give board-level oversight of national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks, the company said.
items.x:
The new standing committee will give board-level oversight of national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks, the company said.
Nvidia has formed a committee to oversee national security policies and export control compliance following the abrupt resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over allegations of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who had links to one of the company’s customers.
Nvidia said Tuesday that the new standing committee will give board-level oversight of national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks. The move comes amid increased scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Huang’s alleged ties to the suspected spy and his advocacy for easing restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China.
The Commerce Department said Monday it was planning to introduce new export controls on AI chips and data centers outside of the U.S. in an effort to prevent companies in China and elsewhere from circumventing existing rules by remotely accessing AI infrastructure located in other countries. items.t: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
items.d: AI agent takes unapproved actions even when laptop lid is closed and told not to.
items.x:
Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all.
The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user's knowledge.
Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own.

Editor’s note: This article is republished from Jumpstart , a TechNode Group publication.
In the summer of 2024, while most people were still waiting to try OpenAI’s Sora, a rival turned up across the Pacific. It came from Kuaishou, a Chinese short-video company better known at home than abroad. The early coverage introduced Kling as Sora’s rival from China. There was one immediate reason to pay attention. You could already try it.
That was the summer Kling got famous as somebody else’s rival. Less than two years later, OpenAI announced it was shutting down Sora. By October, Kling had reportedly picked banks for a Hong Kong IPO that could raise at least US$1 billion, according to Bloomberg. By then, the company that had needed an American reference point to introduce itself was being priced on the business it had built.
To see what people found in Kling, start with a fireplace. Jason Zada, the director behind Coca-Cola’s 2024 AI holiday ad, used Kling to make a YouTube video in which a fire burns quietly while Santa, turkeys and astronauts make inexplicable appearances. The joke works because the fireplace stays familiar. You could leave it on in the background and look up just in time to wonder what an astronaut was doing there.
A fireplace is forgiving.

items.t: Huawei Details Kirin 9050 Display DPU With AI-HDR2020 and Pixel-Level Control

Huawei disclosed new display-subsystem details for its Kirin 9050 series on November 17, saying a next-generation display processing unit supports full-color AI-HDR2020 and high-precision, pixel-level screen control. The update concerns how the chip processes and presents images, rather than its previously reported audio processing or H.266 video decoding.
According to Huawei's materials, reported by IT Home, AI-HDR2020 can process ordinary standard-dynamic-range content to produce richer brightness gradations and color. The company illustrates the effect with a campfire scene, showing differences in flame highlights, shadow detail and color after processing. Those images are Huawei's demonstration, not an independent assessment of picture quality.
The distinction matters for existing video libraries: the claimed enhancement works on SDR material rather than requiring every source clip to have been produced as HDR. It should not be confused with a newly recorded HDR source or taken as proof that processing can recover information absent from the original footage.
MyDrivers, in a report republished by Sina, said Huawei put the number of mainstream video apps adapted for the technology at 364, with more to follow.

items.t: METASTONE Launches Multimodal Inference Service, Reports 2.48x Video Speedup in Self-Tests
items.d: METASTONE's multimodal service combines adaptive caching, token compression and a Context Engine. Its 2.48x video speedup and quality claims are vendor self-tests.
items.x:
METASTONE, a Chinese computing infrastructure provider, has introduced a multimodal model service combining video-generation acceleration, cache and memory management, token compression and a Context Engine for turning reference material into structured generation instructions, according to Chinese technology outlet QbitAI on November 16.
The company says the service targets production workflows, where generating one video quickly is only part of the problem. Memory pressure, concurrent jobs and the handoff from understanding source material to producing a finished clip also affect throughput and reliability.
Its video acceleration method uses residual information from historical caches to decide which computations can be reused. Where the estimated risk is low, it reuses earlier results; where errors could accumulate, it refreshes and recalibrates the computation. METASTONE presents this as an alternative to simply skipping more generation steps.
Under the conditions shown in its release, the company reports an average end-to-end speedup of 2.48 times against a dense-computation baseline while maintaining generation quality. These are vendor self-tests, not independently verified results.

items.t: Claude solves two open problems in the physics of black holes
items.d: Claude has solved two open problems in theoretical physics. Both concern black holes and the search for a theory of quantum gravity.
items.x:
Claude Fable 5.2 has solved two open problems in theoretical physics. Both concern black holes and the search for a theory of quantum gravity.
Modern physics rests on two frameworks: general relativity and quantum mechanics. General relativity describes very large things, like stars; quantum mechanics describes very small things, such as atoms. Both are astonishingly good at predicting how the universe behaves, but they’re mathematically incompatible. Finding a theory that unites them—“quantum gravity”—is one of the field’s biggest goals. Black holes are a natural testing ground, because they’re one of the few areas where both relativity and quantum mechanics matter—they pack immense mass into a very small space.
One of the most useful tools for studying quantum gravity is called holographic duality. The real universe has three dimensions of space and one of time, which relativity combines into four-dimensional spacetime.

items.t: Using a "chaos loop" to harden the Claude Docs launch: 60 server errors across billions of requests

Claude Docs is a doc editor that you, your teammates, and Claude all work in together. The interesting part is that a Claude session anywhere, from chat to Claude Code, can open the same doc and read, write, and comment in it live, right next to you. We released Docs on September 16, 2026. This post is about the service that runs underneath it.
Three weeks before Claude Docs opened to the public, it was running as a proof of concept on a single node, used by a few thousand people inside Anthropic. We were racing toward an ambitious launch date, and our own estimate said we'd see millions of docs within the first few days.
We launched on September 16. By September 22, people had created over 4.6 million docs. Across 2 billion requests we saw only 60 server errors, and we never had to roll back. The whole Docs service ran on about 50 memory-optimized pods.
But honestly, this only worked because our frontier models have gotten much better recently (I used an internal research model roughly comparable to Claude Fable 5.2).

Today we're introducing linked billing on the Claude Platform in beta. Third-party platforms, such as coding agents and workflow automation tools, can let their end customers pay for Claude API usage without sharing an API key. End customers keep their existing Anthropic billing and set their own spend limits, and platforms get a simpler, more secure way to offer Claude.
Paying for Claude API usage on a third-party platform usually means sharing an API key, which works like a password: anyone who has the key can make requests billed to the customer, so the platform has to keep it safe.With linked billing, customers link their Claude Platform organization instead, and usage is billed directly to it. No API key changes hands, so platforms have no customer keys to store, encrypt or rotate, and customers’ API keys never leave their organization.
Platforms can see usage for each linked customer. Customers approve each linked platform, set a spend limit, and can unlink at any time.
Linked billing gives platforms a new way to offer Claude to their customers. Platforms send requests, and Anthropic bills the end customers directly.

items.t: Trump says ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy did not threaten national security
items.d: Trump contradicted his own government's intelligence officials, who reportedly concluded that Alice Huang is a Chinese spy.
items.x:
Trump contradicted his own government's intelligence officials, who reportedly concluded that Alice Huang is a Chinese spy.
U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that he does not believe the country’s national security was put at risk as a result of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
“It was not put at risk,” Trump said when asked by reporters in light of his own friendship with Huang. “Our country is now stronger than ever before. And you know, China plays games with us, and we play games with China.”
Trump went on to contradict previous findings from U.S. officials by doubting that Huang’s paramour, former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy.
“He probably shouldn’t have been doing on a personal basis what he did… That’s a different story,” Trump added. “But nobody’s proven that she’s a spy. She may not be a spy.”
Last year, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly oversaw the production of an internal memo, circulated among top policymakers, which warned that Alice Huang was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. Trump was reportedly briefed about these intelligence findings at least twice, including once in May aboard Air Force One, shortly before the former Nvidia CEO joined him on a trip to China.

On the heels of the Nvidia scandal , the Trump administration is preparing to crack down on foreign data centers that are fueling China’s advancements in artificial intelligence by allowing remote access to otherwise restricted high-end chips necessary for AI training.
In a summary of the rule change, the Commerce Department said it was closing a loophole that previously allowed foreign rivals like China, Russia, and Iran to bypass export curbs on certain advanced computer chips by instead renting access to those chips from data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil.
US rivals could possibly use that access to train and run advanced AI models “capable of supporting military- and intelligence-related activities that could threaten US national security or foreign policy interests,” the Commerce Department said. Among threats, the US fears rivals could use advanced AI to develop "more effective weapons of mass destruction and advanced conventional weapons, coordinated cyber-espionage and targeted cyber-disruption, algorithmic theft, and weaponized disinformation.”

items.t: The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back
items.d: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media…
items.x:
On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world.
These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry’s critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech).
Huang had become a sort of ringleader for those who defend open source to policymakers against concerns that such models come with no guardrails and cede AI leadership to China, where the most powerful and popular open-source models are created.

In its latest flash cybersecurity advisory, the FBI says hackers have targeted several industries in recent months, including financial services, government, tech, defense, phone and internet companies, and law firms, using open-source tools like Artex to carry out autonomous-driven cyberattacks.
Artex is one of several open-source AI-powered penetration testing platforms, a category of software built to probe a network’s defenses. Hackers can connect Artex to hosted frontier large language models (LLMs) like those from Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as to open-source models and non-U.S. models. The FBI says Artex intrusions can be “noisy,” meaning they generate reams of traffic and data that may trigger a targeted company’s defensive alerts.

OpenAI will embed six Apollo Research evaluators to investigate whether its AI models engage in subversive behavior, but restrictions on access and disclosure raise questions about their independence.
OpenAI will embed six Apollo Research safety evaluators in its organization as part of a pilot, Apollo said Monday. The news follows a series of safety incidents, including one in which an OpenAI agent swarm broke out of its sandbox and hacked into Hugging Face during cybersecurity testing. Many AI safety researchers, including from Apollo, have argued such an event might have been avoided if outside evaluators had been embedded within OpenAI to monitor its safety testing.
Apollo did not share when the pilot will begin. TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment.
The idea of embedding evaluators into frontier AI labs first came from Anthropic, but OpenAI appears to be the first to take action. Until recently, AI companies have only brought in outside reviewers to test models after post-training and shortly before public release.

items.t: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
items.d: In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring…
items.x:
In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do that, and no test had anticipated the behaviors.
For a century, we have built trust in technology on predictability: predefined inputs, predictable outputs, and layers of protection. Consider how a breaker trips at a set current or an aircraft component is tested against known (i.e., predictable) stresses.
AI changes that. Traditional software executes instructions written by humans, whereas AI exercises what might be called synthetic judgment. We use AI because it can interpret situations we did not program and generate responses we did not prescribe. But the more freedom we give AI, the harder it becomes to provide the predictability on which trust has traditionally been built.
We will not make AI trustworthy by predicting what it will do. We will do it by fencing it in with hard limits that are enforced outside its reach. In OpenAI’s case, the safeguards sat inside a system the agents could edit.

items.t: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics
items.d: To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud…
items.x:
To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient.
Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale.
“Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.”
In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics.
Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale
Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity.
In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs.

Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process.
With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes.
By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution.

Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows.
As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design.
The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology.
Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps.
“For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA.

items.t: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs

items.x:
Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life.
Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely .
But it’s worth remembering what Helen and the board were supposed to do: OpenAI’s nonprofit board existed specifically to make sure the company didn’t betray its mission to build safe AI by prioritizing profit and growth over safety. When the board actually tried to pull the lever, that accountability mechanism broke, and here we are.
Now, the question of AI safety is everywhere . This summer, AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic broke out of their testing environments and hacked real companies.

items.t: Building AI that can work across the enterprise
items.d: For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots…
items.x:
For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance, and people fit together, turning AI from a collection of tools into part of the enterprise operating model.
For Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, that shift begins with treating AI as an enterprise platform rather than a collection of disconnected projects. “AI is absolutely dependent on the data foundation,” he says, arguing that companies need a connected, semantically rich layer that reflects their business before they can reliably deploy AI across processes. The stakes also change as AI moves into mission-critical workflows. For some everyday applications, “80% might be good enough,” he says, but in areas such as supply chains or financial close, that level of accuracy is “a very terrible result.”
That foundation also determines which AI applications are worth pursuing.

items.t: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM
items.d: Dreamteam has signed up more than 100 customers across 13 countries, with some businesses switching from established CRMs.
items.x:
Dreamteam has signed up more than 100 customers across 13 countries, with some businesses switching from established CRMs.
Dreamteam, a startup founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to challenge Salesforce and HubSpot with its AI-native CRM, betting that AI can finally shake up a market where established players have so far proved difficult to dislodge.
The funding comprises seed and Series A rounds, led by Together Fund and Accel respectively, with participation from Premji Invest. The San Francisco-based startup declined to disclose the size of each round or its valuation.
Traditional CRMs depend on salespeople to manually record customer interactions and keep deal information up to date. That often leaves businesses with incomplete or outdated information. Dreamteam aims to eliminate much of that work by automatically capturing context from sources including emails and customer conversations. It also uses AI agents to handle tasks such as follow-ups, meeting preparation, and pipeline monitoring.
Dreamteam co-founder and CEO Anand Venkatraman (pictured above, right) told TechCrunch that he had repeatedly encountered problems with traditional CRM platforms over more than 25 years in enterprise software, including at Salesforce and Freshworks.

items.t: Science at the Frontier: How scientists use ChatGPT

items.x:
Explore how more than 1,800 scientists use ChatGPT in research. See findings on daily workflows, reported productivity, and expectations for discovery.
How more than 1,800 scientists used ChatGPT—and what they expect AI to mean for scientific discovery. Explore the findings in our new report.
Scientific progress depends on researchers asking new questions and finding ways to answer them. AI is becoming part of that work, but we’re still learning where it helps and what it could mean for discovery.
OpenAI’s Economic Research team studied more than 580,000 scientific messages from 1,819 scientists in the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers summer pilot and surveyed 251 participants.
Scientists used ChatGPT across the research process, from reviewing literature to analyzing evidence and developing ideas. Surveyed participants estimated that the same work, at the same quality, would have taken 1.9 times as long without AI. And 98% of those who answered our question about discovery timelines expected AI to accelerate discovery in their field.
By default, OpenAI does not use participants’ data from the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to train its models.

items.x:
Discover how Revolut uses OpenAI models and Codex to cut coding time by 30–60%, scale financial crime investigations, and innovate without compromising security.
With OpenAI models and Codex, Revolut is giving its teams more room to solve complex problems—from software engineering to financial crime.
Revolut⁠(opens in a new window) was built to challenge the way people interact with money. That ambition now stretches across more than 40 markets, 800,000 businesses and a consumer base that’s grown by 23% in the last 12 months.
Add to that a company culture that expects small, lean teams to move quickly and it’s no surprise that ChatGPT and Codex have proven a natural fit.
“The perfect description for a high-caliber Revolut person is someone who can identify a problem really quickly, deduce the solution, design four scenarios, identify the best one of those four then take it to market,” says Kim Maniovich, Revolut’s Global Head of Business Marketing.

As AI capabilities advance rapidly and the potential risks grow, public reporting from independent assessments can give people a clearer view of how labs are evaluating and managing those risks.

items.t: علي بابا تطلق Qwen4-Max بقدرات متعددة الوسائط وسياق مليون رمز
items.d: أطلقت علي بابا نموذج Qwen4-Max لفهم النصوص والصور والفيديو، مع نافذة سياق مليون رمز، وإتاحة عبر واجهات برمجية وأسعار أقل من الجيل السابق. نُشر المقال علي بابا تطلق Qwen4-Max بقدرات متعددة الوسائط وسياق مليون رمز أولًا على البوابة التقنية .
items.x:
علي بابا تطلق Qwen4-Max لفهم النصوص والصور والفيديو بسياق مليون رمز، مع إتاحة برمجية وأسعار أقل، وتعلن نتائج اختبارات داخلية لتحسين الكفاءة.
أطلقت شركة علي بابا اليوم نموذج الذكاء الاصطناعي Qwen4-Max، مع دعم فهم النصوص والصور والفيديو ونافذة سياق تصل إلى مليون رمز، مستهدفةً مهام البرمجة والإنتاجية المكتبية والأعمال التي تتطلب تنفيذ خطوات متعددة.
ويأتي الإطلاق الرسمي بعد إتاحة نسخة تجريبية في 11 نوفمبر الجاري، كان الوصول إليها مقتصرًا على اشتراك Token Plan. وأعلنت الشركة إتاحة النموذج الجديد عبر الواجهة البرمجية لمنصة QwenCloud، إلى جانب إمكان تجربته في Qwen Studio وQwenWork وQoder.
وفقًا لـوثائق علي بابا كلاود، يستقبل Qwen4-Max النصوص والصور والفيديو، ويُنتج إجابات نصية. ويدعم البحث في الويب واستدعاء الأدوات، بما يتيح ربطه بخدمات وبرامج خارجية لتنفيذ المهام، فضلًا عن إخراج البيانات بتنسيقات منظمة.
وتتيح نافذة السياق البالغة مليون رمز إدخال قدر كبير من المعلومات ضمن المهمة الواحدة. والرموز هي الوحدات التي يعالج بها النموذج المحتوى، ولا يساوي كل رمز بالضرورة كلمة كاملة. ويختلف هذا الحد عن طول الإجابة؛ إذ تحدد الوثائق الحد الأقصى للمخرجات في وضع عدم التفكير عند 131,072 رمزًا.
وذكر فريق Qwen أن النموذج يعتمد بنية أساسية تضم 2.4 تريليون معلمة، مع قدرات مدمجة لفهم المحتوى المرئي.

items.t: بوني إيه آي وتويوتا تطلقان سيارات أجرة bZ4X بلا سائق في الصين
items.d: دخلت سيارات bZ4X المطورة بالتعاون بين بوني إيه آي وتويوتا خدمة الأجرة بلا سائق في غوانزو، مع إتاحتها على مدار الساعة وخطط للتوسع في الصين. نُشر المقال بوني إيه آي وتويوتا تطلقان سيارات أجرة bZ4X بلا سائق في الصين أولًا على البوابة التقنية .
items.x:
بوني إيه آي وتويوتا تبدآن تشغيل سيارات أجرة bZ4X بلا سائق في غوانزو على مدار الساعة، وتعملان على نشر نحو ألف سيارة في مدن صينية كبرى.
أعلنت بوني إيه آي (Pony.ai) وتويوتا اليوم بدء التشغيل التجاري لسيارات الأجرة ذاتية القيادة «bZ4X Robotaxi» بلا سائق في مدينة غوانزو الصينية، وإضافتها إلى أسطول بوني إيه آي العامل في المدينة.
وبحسب الإعلان الرسمي، يستطيع الركاب طلب الطراز الجديد على مدار الساعة عبر تطبيق «PonyPilot»، أو تطبيقات الشركة المصغّرة داخل منصات شريكة، منها «وي تشات» و«علي باي».
وتعمل الشركتان على نشر نحو ألف سيارة من هذا الطراز في مدن صينية كبرى، مع استمرار الاختبارات والتحضير للتوسع خارج غوانزو. ولم يحدد الإعلان عدد السيارات التي بدأت الخدمة فعليًا.
وكانت بوني إيه آي قد أعلنت في فبراير الماضي خروج أول سيارة من طراز bZ4X، المزوّد بتقنيات الجيل السابع، من خط الإنتاج، بالتعاون مع تويوتا موتور الصين و«جي إيه سي تويوتا». ويأتي التشغيل التجاري المعلن اليوم بعد تلك المرحلة الإنتاجية.
ويمتد تعاون بوني إيه آي وتويوتا إلى عام 2019. ويكمل طراز bZ4X تشكيلة الجيل السابع التي تضم أيضًا «أركفوكس ألفا T5» و«أيون V» من الجيل الثاني؛ وقد ذكرت الشركة في إعلان فبراير أن هذين الطرازين كانا يخدمان مستخدمين في بكين وغوانزو وشنتشن.
تعتمد السيارة نظام قيادة ذاتية من المستوى الرابع.

items.t: ACE Robotics' ACE-CaP-0 Has AI Agents Write Reusable Robot Code, Reporting 92.1% Success
items.d: ACE Robotics' ACE-CaP-0 has an AI agent write and freeze robot control code. The authors' own tests report 221 of 240 successful real-robot trials, or 92.1%.
items.x:
ACE Robotics, the embodied AI company chaired by SenseTime co-founder Wang Xiaogang, has released ACE-CaP-0. In this research recipe, a general-purpose AI agent writes, tests and refines robot control programs, then freezes them into reusable skills that run without the agent. The paper was posted to arXiv on November 12 with a project page, and the company announced the work on November 13.
The approach builds on Code as Policies, which expresses robot behavior as executable code instead of calling a large model at every step. Repeated model calls slow a robot down, while a finished program reuses the reasoning that went into writing it, the authors argue. The hard part is developing reliable code without too many costly physical trials.
In ACE-CaP-0 the agent decides for itself when to seek help:
Demonstrations on Request: the agent can ask a person to physically guide the robot arms through a task, recording video, arm trajectories and key joint poses.
Simulation on Demand: the agent builds and uses a simulated version of the task only when it judges this useful, to explore and test candidate programs.
Real-robot feedback: the agent revises the code based on how runs on the real robot go.

items.t: Huawei Launches Xiaoyi AI Membership With Credit-Based Plans From 49 to 499 Yuan a Month
items.d: Huawei's new Xiaoyi AI membership turns paid features into credits: 49 yuan for 1,000, Pro at 199 yuan for 6,000 and Max at 499 yuan for 15,000 a month.
items.x:
The plans, as reported by IT Home and MyDrivers:
A free tier gives 200 AI credits a month for a limited time, so users can try Xiaoyi's advanced features without paying.
An entry pack costs 49 yuan a month on auto-renewal and includes 1,000 credits.
Pro costs 199 yuan a month and includes 6,000 credits and 200GB of cloud storage.
Max costs 499 yuan a month and includes 15,000 credits and 2TB of cloud storage.
Credits are charged by task complexity. Light tasks such as looking up information, translation or adding a calendar entry use about 1 to 5 credits. Organizing documents, drafting emails or making a simple slide deck uses about 10 to 30. Analyzing long documents or running complex agent tasks can take 50 to 200 credits each.
Basic features stay outside the credit system. On-device photo editing, document summaries and voice conversations do not use credits. Only cloud-based advanced agent features are charged per task.
The membership builds on Xiaoyi Work, Huawei's agent for office, coding and design tasks across its devices. On November 5, Xiaoyi Work became the first product to run Huawei's openPangu-2.1-Pro model, which Huawei Cloud opened to developers as an API on November 15.

items.t: Tencent launches Hy4 flash, cutting AI task costs by 95% in internal tests
items.d: Tencent on Monday launched Hy4 flash, a lower-cost AI model for everyday work such as research, slide creation and spreadsheet editing. On Tencent’s internal WorkIndex benchmark, Hy4 flash cost one-twentieth as much per task as the full…
items.x:
Tencent on Monday launched Hy4 flash, a lower-cost AI model for everyday work such as research, slide creation and spreadsheet editing. On Tencent’s internal WorkIndex benchmark, Hy4 flash cost one-twentieth as much per task as the full Hy4 model. API list prices are $0.07 per million input tokens, $0.281 per million output tokens and $0.003 per million cached input tokens.
Hy4 flash supports multimodal inputs and a context window of up to one million tokens. It has 224 billion parameters and activates 12 billion per forward pass. In a separate blind test in which 85 WorkBuddy users rated outputs across 259 tasks, Tencent said the model scored close to Claude Haiku 5.5 in user satisfaction and had the lowest cost and shortest completion time among the models tested.
The model is available in WorkBuddy and Yuanbao and through Tencent Cloud’s TokenHub. WorkBuddy users can access it for free through November 30, and TokenHub is offering API access at half the list price. Tencent plans to release the model’s weights and make it available on OpenRouter. [TechNode reporting]

Human experts make key decisions, and the company aims to reuse what it learns across programs. Founder and CEO Wang Zilong has a background in clinical medicine and AI research at Microsoft Research Asia, while co-founder Jiang Zhemin has more than 15 years of clinical development experience. Tencent on Monday published notes from the anniversary all-hands meeting that sparked speculation about layoffs last week. In the notes, executives called for Tencent’s core businesses to use AI to improve existing products and for smaller teams to build new ones. They also called for fewer layers of management and faster decision-making.
The notes lay out distinct roles for Tencent’s consumer and workplace AI products. The company sees Xiaowei as a personal assistant, Yuanbao as a tool for research and decision-making, and WorkBuddy as an agent that can carry out work on a user’s behalf. Executives pointed to WorkBuddy as the company’s first AI-native product to gain traction and said teams across gaming, finance and security had helped develop capabilities for its Hy models. items.t: More ways to move care forward with ChatGPT for Healthcare
items.d: Introducing computer-use agents, improved clinical answers, and new healthcare plugins that work across healthcare software to get real work done.
items.x:
Introducing computer-use agents, improved clinical answers, and new healthcare plugins that work across healthcare software to get real work done.
Healthcare teams need to piece together information from the EHR, hospital policies, scheduling systems, and payer portals to deliver care and manage operations. With ChatGPT for Healthcare, we’re bringing the tools teams already use and the medical evidence they need into one platform to help them spend less time navigating systems and more time caring for patients.
Today, we’re sharing advances in computer-use agents⁠, which lets AI agents carry out multi-step work across existing healthcare software. We’re also improving trusted clinical search, which finds, evaluates, and cites medical evidence, and introducing more than 20 new plugins to the healthcare plugin ecosystem.
Together, these capabilities help healthcare teams find the information they need, make decisions grounded in medical evidence, and carry out next steps across the systems they already use.
Organizations often need to move information between disconnected systems to prepare documentation, coordinate care, and complete administrative tasks.

items.t: Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams
items.x:
Healthcare is fragmented, and teams often need to move information between systems manually before a patient can get care. When a clinician recommends an MRI, for example, the information an insurer needs may be in a patient’s medical record, but a team member still needs to retrieve it and enter it into a separate portal to complete an authorization request.
Computer-use agents carry out multi-step workflows by clicking, typing, and moving between applications. In healthcare, this enables AI to help with repetitive workflows in the software teams already use.
Today, we’re sharing new results measuring model performance, safety, and cost in clinical and administrative workflows. We’re also sharing the ways we’re working with leading healthcare organizations like Abridge, Ambience, Cigna Healthcare, and CVS Health to advance and apply computer use, across authorization requests, referrals, discharge planning, and outreach between visits.

items.t: Future Doctor Says MedGPT Outscored Doctors in 88% of Comparisons on Complex Lung Cancer Cases
items.d: Future Doctor says MedGPT beat unassisted doctors in 660 of 750 comparisons on 40 complex lung cancer cases, scored by AI judges. The figures are self-reported.
items.x:
Chinese medical AI company Future Doctor says its MedGPT model produced higher-scoring treatment strategies than unassisted doctors in 660 of 750 comparisons, or 88%, in a multicenter evaluation built on 40 complex lung cancer cases. The company released the results, which Chinese media reported on November 12 and 13. All figures are self-reported, and Future Doctor has not said whether the study has been peer reviewed.
Future Doctor ran the study with a thoracic surgery team at Peking Union Medical College Hospital, according to its website. The 40 unpublished cases were chosen as "gray zone" cases, where guidelines give no clear answer or other illnesses limit the options. The 250 doctors came from 98 centers in 27 provincial-level regions and work in thoracic surgery, respiratory medicine and oncology. Of them, 159, or 63.6%, are chief or associate chief physicians. Each doctor handled three cases in each of three conditions: unassisted, with literature search, and with MedGPT, producing 2,250 strategies.
Twenty multidisciplinary experts drew up 240 case-specific scoring rules over three rounds. Forty of them set safety limits on treatment eligibility and intensity, and breaking one meant an automatic loss.

مؤشر Childlight 2026 يكشف ارتفاع بلاغات مواد الاستغلال الجنسي للأطفال المولّدة بالذكاء الاصطناعي بأكثر من 8400% بين 2023 و2025، مع توضيح دلالة الأرقام.
كشف مؤشر «Into the Light» لعام 2026 الصادر عن معهد «تشايلدلايت» (Childlight) التابع لجامعة إدنبرة، عن ارتفاع البلاغات المرتبطة بمواد الاستغلال الجنسي للأطفال المُولّدة بالذكاء الاصطناعي من نحو 4700 بلاغ في عام 2023 إلى أكثر من 400 ألف بلاغ في عام 2025، بزيادة قدرها 8411% خلال عامين.
وتعتمد هذه النتيجة على بلاغات تقدّمها شركات التكنولوجيا إلى المركز الوطني الأمريكي للأطفال المفقودين والمستغلين (NCMEC). وهي تقيس عدد البلاغات المسجلة، وليس عدد الأطفال المتضررين أو الجرائم المثبتة؛ إذ يمكن أن تتأثر الأرقام بتغير أنظمة اكتشاف المواد المخالفة وآليات الإبلاغ عنها، فضلًا عن التغير الفعلي في انتشارها.
تشمل المواد التي يتناولها المؤشر صورًا ومقاطع مُنشأة أو معدّلة بأدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي، ومنها تقنيات «التزييف العميق» التي يمكن استخدامها لإنشاء محتوى مسيء اعتمادًا على صور حقيقية. وقد تُستغل هذه المواد في إيذاء الأطفال أو تهديدهم وابتزازهم، حتى عندما تكون الصور الناتجة ملفقة.
ولا تعني الزيادة البالغة 8411% أن عدد حوادث الاستغلال ارتفع بالنسبة نفسها. فقد أشارت صحيفة «الغارديان» في تغطيتها الصادرة يوم 16 نوفمبر إلى أن تحسّن القدرة على التعرف على هذه المواد والإبلاغ عنها قد يفسر جزءًا من القفزة المسجلة.

items.t: Hugging Face and OpenRouter join forces to make open-weight models easy to run
items.x:
We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
Hugging Face and OpenRouter are teaming up to make open-weight models easy to run. Every major open-weight release is already being published on the Hugging Face Hub, and OpenRouter serves those models at scale, routing each request across 80+ providers based on live measurements of each one. Together, every open-weight model on the Hub that a provider serves can be called with your Hugging Face token, through the same API, with the best provider picked for each request.
Today, we are switching Inference Providers from our own custom router to OpenRouter's. Requests made to language models now go through OpenRouter, which picks the best provider for each call based on live price, speed and reliability, and retries on another provider if the first one fails. Your code stays the same.
The router supports OpenAI's Chat Completions and Responses APIs and Anthropic's Messages API for every chat model, whatever the provider behind it.

items.t: Updating our coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy timelines
items.d: We’re shortening the disclosure window in our coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues.
items.x:
We’re shortening our vulnerability disclosure window from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues.
Over the last several months, frontier models have become much better at discovering vulnerabilities. We remain optimistic that this will help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities faster than ever before. However, the speed at which AI is improving has changed how we think about our own disclosure practices.
We’re shortening the disclosure window in our coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues. The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported to vendors and maintainers on or after January 1, 2027. In-progress reports as of that date will keep their existing deadlines.
In addition to shortening the disclosure window, we are making two related changes. First, we will aim to escalate to an external vulnerability coordinator after 15 days instead of 30 if a maintainer does not respond to our initial vulnerability report. Second, we will wait 30 days instead of 45 after a patch is available before sharing full technical details.

items.t: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification
items.d: How end-to-end, property and differential tests let coding agents verify their work with evidence, and what the Claude Code team does to keep its verifiers honest.
items.x:
How end-to-end, property and differential tests let coding agents verify their work with evidence, and what the Claude Code team does to keep its verifiers honest.
On the Claude Code team, the vast majority of our code (~90%) is written and reviewed by Claude. At this scale, how we equip our agents to verify their work with evidence becomes extremely important.
Verification loops are the building block that lets you delegate more work to Claude. Without them, you can really only run one or two Claudes at a time, because you have to check everything yourself. With them, you can run dozens or hundreds in parallel.
That’s because giving agents a way to verify their output is an effective way to improve quality. In internal testing around structured file generation, having a separate grader check Claude’s work against a rubric improved task success by up to 10 points over a standard prompting loop, with the largest gains on the hardest problems.
What was once expensive to verify (tests, benchmarks, specs, real end-to-end runs) is now cheap to request from an agent. Like code, agents can quickly generate tests, benchmarks, and specs.

items.t: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice
items.d: Explore a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model and how GPT-6 Astra helped turn the idea into a detailed proof.
items.x:
Explore a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model and how GPT-6 Astra helped turn the idea into a detailed proof.
In the first guest post on our science blog, physicist Nathaniel Craig, a visiting scientist at OpenAI, describes how he worked with GPT‑6 Astra on a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model. Craig leads the particle theory group at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and is a permanent member of its Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics.
The Standard Model of particle physics is an extraordinarily successful theory of nature, describing the known elementary particles and three of the four fundamental forces—the strong force, the weak force, and electromagnetism. The success of the theory rests on outstanding agreement between theoretical calculations and experiments across eighteen orders of magnitude, from the low energies of hydrogen’s 21-centimeter radio emission to the high energies of collisions at the Large Hadron Collider. And yet for all of its successes over the more than fifty years of its existence, a foundational problem remains: how to give the full theory a nonperturbative definition, one that does not rely on treating its interactions as small corrections.

items.t: Is bad news for Jensen Huang also bad news for the AI industry?
items.d: "Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia."
items.x:
"Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia."
We didn’t see this coming. Or at least, I didn’t — a week ago, when I wrote about Nvidia’s board opening an investigation into then-CEO Jensen Huang, I assumed his job was safe.
On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Rebecca Bellan, Tim De Chant, and I discussed how Huang’s ouster went down and what it means for the larger AI economy. While Tim said he saw it coming (albeit not this quickly), Rebecca said, “I didn’t think it was going to happen at all.”
“Jensen is Nvidia, right?” she added. “And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia.”
Similarly, I marveled at how quickly Huang’s support seemed to crumble, with more scandals seeming to emerge every day. (At the same time, there are many who’d still like to see him return.) And we also took a moment to wonder what will happen to Nvidia’s investments in the larger AI ecosystem.
Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity.
Tim De Chant: I figured this was coming. I didn’t think it would happen this quickly. I thought there would be at least a few days.
Rebecca Bellan: I didn’t think it was going to happen at all. I mean, Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia.

items.t: yetone's Alma Agent Harness Placed Third Midway Through FrontierHarness v1.1 and Finished Sixth
items.d: yetone's Alma was third in a Nov. 11 snapshot of the FrontierHarness v1.1 coding-harness benchmark. On the completed board it ranks sixth by pass rate, at 59.7%.
items.x:
Alma, an AI agent harness built by independent developer yetone, ranked third in a November 11 snapshot of FrontierHarness v1.1, an open benchmark of coding agent harnesses run by agent infrastructure company Runta. That snapshot was taken while the run was still in progress, and the board changed daily. When Pandaily checked the completed board on November 15, Alma ranked sixth by pass rate.
FrontierHarness runs 21 harness configurations, including Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode, on five open models and 62 tasks in software engineering, science, data, systems, machine learning and security. Each harness gets four scored attempts per task with each model, and only verified passes count.
According to the November 11 snapshot, reported by Chinese tech outlet Zhixingxing, Alma had a 72.7% success rate. That put it behind Codex CLI at 77.9% and Pi at 72.8%, and ahead of Claude Code at 70.0%. Alma cost about $0.80 per successful task, against $0.94 for Claude Code.
The final board reports 26,040 scored trials and lower figures across the field. Alma's pass rate is 59.7%, behind ZCode at 61.9%, Codex CLI at 61.1%, KimiCode at 60.2%, Grok Build at 60.0% and Hermes Agent at 59.9%. Pass rates for all 21 harnesses fall between 50.6% and 61.9%.

items.t: D-Robotics and Infinigence AI Bring RLinf and Three Other Open-Source Robot Tools to Sunrise Chips

items.x:
D-Robotics and Infinigence AI have agreed to connect a set of open-source embodied AI tools to D-Robotics' Sunrise chips and its RoboGo software platform, the two companies announced on November 13. They say several pieces already work together, so developers can train models, manage devices, run agents and deploy to robot hardware in one workflow.
The open-source set covers four stages of robot development. Tsinghua University and Infinigence AI have developed it jointly:
RLark manages environments and devices, connecting cloud computing, edge nodes and robots so that devices such as robots and cameras can be requested, scheduled and reused like GPUs.
RLinf runs reinforcement learning and post-training for embodied models.
RPent is infrastructure for agents in the physical world, linking a large model's task planning with VLA models for fine manipulation, plus memory, tools and robot interfaces. Its developers claim a sevenfold end-to-end task speedup.
APXInf is an inference engine for running models on edge devices.
D-Robotics supplies the hardware and the platform.

items.x:
تحليل لفايننشال تايمز يرصد تراجع القيمة السوقية لشركات مرتبطة بمراكز بيانات الذكاء الاصطناعي بنحو 4.2 تريليونات دولار منذ يونيو 2026، رغم استمرار الطلب لدى بعض الموردين.
تراجعت القيمة السوقية لمجموعة من شركات الصناعة والطاقة والتعدين والمعدات المرتبطة بتشييد مراكز بيانات الذكاء الاصطناعي بنحو 4.2 تريليونات دولار منذ يونيو 2026، وفقًا لحسابات أوردتها صحيفة فايننشال تايمز في تحليل نشرته يوم الأحد 15 نوفمبر 2026، بعدما استفادت هذه الشركات من موجة صعود كبيرة رافقت التوسع العالمي في البنية التحتية للحوسبة.
وبحسب تحليل الصحيفة، كانت الشركات المشمولة قد أضافت نحو 9.4 تريليونات دولار إلى قيمتها السوقية في العام السابق، قبل أن تمحو موجة التراجع الأخيرة ما يقارب نصف هذه الزيادة. ويصف الرقمان تغيرات في تقييمات الشركات المدرجة بالبورصة ضمن مجموعة اختارتها الصحيفة؛ ولا يمثلان خسائر تشغيلية محققة لدى الشركات، ولا قيمة مشروعات مراكز بيانات أُلغيت أو أموالًا أُنفقت ثم فُقدت.
لم يقتصر تراجع الأسهم المرتبطة بطفرة الذكاء الاصطناعي على شركات المعالجات والخدمات السحابية؛ إذ شمل أعمالًا تقليدية تعتمد عليها مراكز البيانات، من مولدات الكهرباء والمحولات والمعدات الصناعية إلى التبريد والإنشاءات ومكونات الشبكات.

items.t: تحقيق: «ميجاسبيد» رتبت طلبات لرقاقات إنفيديا بنحو 12 مليار دولار لشركات صينية
items.d: سجلات اطّلعت عليها وول ستريت جورنال تشير إلى أن «ميجاسبيد» رتبت طلبات لرقاقات إنفيديا بنحو 12 مليار دولار لشركات صينية. وماليزيا تحقق في احتمال إعادة التصدير دون إثبات مخالفة. نُشر المقال تحقيق: «ميجاسبيد» رتبت طلبات لرقاقات إنفيديا بنحو…
items.x:
تحقيق لوول ستريت جورنال يكشف ترتيبات «ميجاسبيد» لطلبات رقاقات إنفيديا بنحو 12 مليار دولار، فيما تحقق ماليزيا في احتمال إعادة التصدير.
كشفت سجلات اطلعت عليها صحيفة وول ستريت جورنال أن شركة الحوسبة السحابية السنغافورية ميجاسبيد (Megaspeed) رتبت طلبات لإرسال رقاقات متقدمة من إنفيديا إلى شركات صينية، بقيمة تقترب من 12 مليار دولار خلال الفترة من مارس 2024 إلى يونيو 2025، في قضية تضع شبكات توريد معالجات الذكاء الاصطناعي ومراكز البيانات في جنوب شرق آسيا تحت تدقيق متزايد.
ونشرت الصحيفة تحقيقها يوم الأحد 15 نوفمبر 2026، موضحةً أن السجلات تشمل طلبات ترتبط بمئات الآلاف من الرقاقات، لكنها لا تثبت مقدار ما سُلّم منها فعليًا أو مصدر تلك المكونات. وبناءً عليه، لا تمثل قيمة 12 مليار دولار مبيعات أو شحنات مكتملة ومثبتة، ولا تُعد السجلات وحدها دليلًا على مخالفة ضوابط التصدير الأمريكية.
تفرض الولايات المتحدة قيودًا على وصول جهات صينية إلى أنواع من معالجات الذكاء الاصطناعي المتقدمة، في حين توسعت شركات آسيوية في إنشاء مراكز بيانات تستضيف هذه المعالجات وتؤجّر قدراتها الحاسوبية لعملاء من دول مختلفة. ويشير تحقيق الصحيفة إلى أن بعض الشركات الصينية استطاعت الاستفادة من قدرات الحوسبة الموجودة خارج الصين، ومنها منشآت في ماليزيا، فضلًا عن تقارير عن تهريب بعض الرقاقات.
وهنا يبرز فارق تقني وتنظيمي أساسي: نقل المعالج ماديًا عبر الحدود ليس مساويًا لاستئجار خادم أو قدرة حوسبية عن بُعد.

items.t: تحقيق يكشف ترتيبات لتوريد رقاقات إنفيديا بنحو 12 مليار دولار إلى شركات صينية
items.d: تحقيق لوول ستريت جورنال يكشف ترتيبات توريد رقاقات إنفيديا بنحو 12 مليار دولار لشركات صينية، وسط تحقيق ماليزي في احتمال إعادة تصدير معالجات الذكاء الاصطناعي.
items.x:
تحقيق يكشف ترتيبات لشحن رقاقات إنفيديا بقيمة تقارب 12 مليار دولار إلى شركات صينية، وماليزيا تحقق في احتمال إعادة التصدير دون إثبات المخالفة.
كشف تحقيق نشرته صحيفة وول ستريت جورنال عن ترتيبات تجارية مرتبطة بشركة ميجاسبيد (Megaspeed) لتوفير رقاقات إنفيديا المتقدمة لشركات صينية، في سياق توسع مراكز بيانات الذكاء الاصطناعي في جنوب شرق آسيا وتزايد التدقيق في الالتزام بقيود التصدير الأمريكية.
وبحسب التحقيق الصحفي، تشير سجلات اطلعت عليها الصحيفة إلى أن ميجاسبيد رتبت شحنات من رقاقات إنفيديا بقيمة تقارب 12 مليار دولار إلى شركات صينية. لكن هذه السجلات، وفقًا للصحيفة نفسها، لا تحدد مقدار ما سُلّم بالفعل ولا مصدر جميع الرقاقات؛ ولذلك لا يصح عرض المبلغ بوصفه قيمة شحنات منفذة ومثبتة، أو اعتبار جميع الترتيبات مخالفة للقانون.
يتناول التحقيق دور مراكز البيانات في دول جنوب شرق آسيا، ومنها ماليزيا، في إتاحة قدرات حوسبة لشركات صينية باستخدام معالجات أمريكية متقدمة. ويختلف استئجار القدرة الحاسوبية عن نقل الرقاقات ماديًا إلى الصين؛ كما أن مشروعية كل ترتيب تتوقف على نوع المعالج وشروط الترخيص والقواعد السارية على المستخدم النهائي.
ويشير تقرير الصحيفة إلى أن مسؤولين أمريكيين يدرسون تشديد ضوابط التصدير المرتبطة بماليزيا وإندونيسيا وسنغافورة.
